purpose: Growing operator ledger of PRIMARY-TEXT-verified varṇa readings for the classically-grounded v3 table. Each entry supplies the classical source quote, the two poles, the cosmological/etymological ASSOCIATIONS (kept SEPARATE from the poles — v2's error was folding associations into the liberating pole), and an attested-vs-authored flag. The v3 builder reads this ledger; varṇas present here become classical_review_status=PRIMARY_TEXT_PROVIDED, the rest stay LEXICON_ATTESTED_PENDING_PRIMARY_VERIFICATION.
resonance_framing: RESONANCE refinement, not validated meaning. No ontology, semantic truth, Sanskrit privilege, GENUTILITY_*, or ONTOLOGICAL_SIGNAL.
anti_circularity: Freeze + pre-register before authoring any pole-test words/contexts. Keep attested-vs-authored splits intact.

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Ha = acoustic root of the ethereal (ākāśa) factor, of daytime, of the sun, of svarloka, and of parā-vidyā. Opposite to ha is ṭha, the acoustic root of nighttime, of the moon, of bhúvarloka, and of the kāmamaya kośa. Ha + ao = hao = acoustic root of Shiva in His táṇḍava posture.
verifications.binding: outward / visible vision — fixation on the manifest, physically-seen, outward-facing world
verifications.liberating: intuitional vision (parā-vidyā) — inner, subtle seeing/knowing
verifications.classical_associations: ether (ākāśa) factor; daytime; sun; svarloka; parā-vidyā. OPPOSITE varṇa = ṭha (night, moon, bhúvarloka, kāmamaya kośa). COMPOUND ha+ao = hao = Shiva's táṇḍava. (Associations + an opposite varṇa — NOT an intra-ha polarity.)
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: the associations above. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating SPLIT (outward-visible vs inner-intuitional) is researcher-imposed; motivated partly by making 'happy' cohere — freeze + pre-register before word/context authoring.
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='night/darkness' imported the OPPOSITE varṇa ṭha's domain into ha's cell (category error); v2 also folded the COMPOUND hao's táṇḍava into bare ha.

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Pa = acoustic root of ghṛṇā vṛtti (hatred/revulsion), the FETTER of hatred (one of the eight pāshas), stemming mainly from moha. 'When one's psychic attraction is toward the crude, the mind has a downward tendency (pat/patati) leading to downfall; when the mind moves upward it is anurakti (attraction for the Great), whose consummation is devotion.'
verifications.binding: attraction toward the crude / objects — the downward-pulling pull (pat / patati -> downfall)
verifications.liberating: revulsion OF the ripus — ghṛṇā redirected against the crude/vices (vairāgya-like turning)
verifications.classical_associations: ghṛṇā = the fetter of hatred (one of the eight pāshas: hatred, doubt, fear, shyness, dissemblance, vanity-of-lineage, cultural-superiority, egotism); six ripus = kāma, krodha, lobha, mada, moha, mātsarya; downward attraction (pat) vs upward anurakti -> devotion.
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: pa = ghṛṇā (revulsion), classically a binding FETTER; the downward-attraction vs upward-anurakti contrast. AUTHORED/REINTERPRETED: making revulsion the LIBERATING pole and attraction the BINDING pole PARTIALLY INVERTS the attested assignment (ghṛṇā/hatred is classically the binding fetter).
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 and the source lexicon both place revulsion on the binding side; this operator reading inverts it.

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Ka = acoustic root of the abhiipśātmaka āśā vṛtti (the propensity of hope), which goads creatures — especially humans — to work in various ways. Ka is ALSO the acoustic root of Kārya Brahma (the expressed universe). Etymology: ka (kae + ḍa) = 'that which produces sound'; also 'water' (flowing water; va = water in general); also 'hair grown on the head' (kac = glossy). Ka + iisha = kesha (hair; also Nārāyaṇa). Kārya Brahma (Saguṇarasātmaka Brahma), represented by ka, is the controller of the living world; Buddhist Saṃvṛtti Bodhicitta = the created world = Kārya Brahma (kāpālika: 'Kaṃ saṃvṛtti bodhicittaṃ pālayati').
verifications.binding: āśā as grasping / clinging hope — goaded toward a specific outcome or object; the downward pull of attached desire
verifications.liberating: aspiring hope held WITHOUT attachment — forward-orientation that acts while releasing the grip on the result (oriented toward the Great, not the object)
verifications.classical_associations: ka = Kārya Brahma (the expressed / created universe; Saguṇarasātmaka Brahma; controller of the living world); 'that which produces sound'; 'water' / flowing water (va = water in general); 'hair on the head' (kesha = ka+iisha, also a name of Nārāyaṇa); Buddhist Saṃvṛtti Bodhicitta. These are cosmological / etymological ASSOCIATIONS of ka, NOT poles.
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: ka = āśā vṛtti (hope that goads action) AND ka = Kārya Brahma (expressed universe) + sound/water/hair associations. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating SPLIT of hope (grasping vs non-attached) applies the general attachment principle — the source states āśā goads action but does not itself split it into poles.
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 put the Kārya-Brahma ASSOCIATION ('expressed universe, creation-field, emergence into manifestation') into the LIBERATING POLE — conflating an attested cosmological association with the liberated form of hope (a category error). The liberating pole of āśā is non-attached aspiration, not 'the created universe.'

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: The acoustic root of āśā vṛtti is ka; that of cintā vṛtti (the propensity of worry) is kha. If your train runs late you think not only of the delay but of the probable inconveniences (the host, arriving late for food, deciding to eat near the station) — such consequential thoughts are symbolized by kha. Travelling elsewhere you might reflect on a collapsing brassware industry and whether it could be revived, though you are 'not personally affected' and 'not a direct player in your own thoughts' — such impersonal thoughts are also kha. Kha MEANS 'sky' but is NOT the acoustic root of the sky (that is ha); kha also means 'heaven', but only its CRUDE aspects — the sphere of heaven that transcends the crude is kṣa. Ka = Kārya Brahma is the first consonant; and since ka + ha = kha, kha immediately follows ka in the Indo-Aryan alphabet.
verifications.binding: cintā as anxious rumination — the mind churning over unresolved contingencies and personal consequences (e.g. worrying through the late-train inconveniences), gripping the what-ifs
verifications.liberating: cintā as composed, impersonal reflection — holding an unsettled situation open without forcing premature closure; objective contemplation in which one is 'not a direct player' (e.g. weighing how a failing industry might be revived), reflection without anxious grip
verifications.classical_associations: Paired with ka: ka = āśā (hope) goads action; kha = cintā (worry / objective thought) reflects. kha MEANS 'sky' and 'heaven' but is NOT their acoustic root — the SKY's root is ha; kha = the CRUDE aspects of heaven, while the transcendent sphere = kṣa (ksha). Structurally ka + ha = kha (hence kha follows ka, the first consonant / Kārya Brahma, in the alphabet). These are meanings/associations, NOT poles.
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: kha = cintā vṛtti; the personal (train) vs impersonal (industry) modes; kha ≠ the sky's root (ha is), kha = crude heaven vs kṣa = transcendent heaven; ka + ha = kha. AUTHORED: labelling anxious/gripping rumination as binding and composed impersonal openness as liberating applies the framework's fixation-vs-detachment principle (consistent with the source lexicon); the passage describes both modes as cintā without itself labelling them binding/liberating.
verifications.v2_drift_note: kha is ABSENT from v2 (bridge-unreachable aspirate — reference-only). English G2P renders written 'kh' as ka + ha (two SEPARATE roots = hope + vision), which does NOT reconstruct cintā — a semantic mismatch, even though ka + ha = kha holds structurally in the classical alphabet.

verifications.sanskrit_label: Ceṣṭā (effort / striving to arouse dormant potential)
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Every entity has the potentiality of expression; an animate entity can arouse that dormant potentiality through both internal and external means. If poetic genius lies dormant in someone and he arouses it by applying his will-force, he becomes a renowned poet; if lethargy prevents it, the genius stays unexpressed. The effort made to arouse one's dormant potentiality is called ceṣṭā. Ceṣṭā is one of the psychic vṛttis and is the MAIN CAUSE of mundane development AND spiritual elevation — its value in the mundane and supramundane spheres is immense. Ga, the acoustic root of ceṣṭā, plays an important role in the physical, psychic and spiritual spheres.
verifications.binding: restless striving that cannot stop — effort compulsively driven on, unable to cease (and, clung to mundane ends, ceaseless outward striving)
verifications.liberating: will-force applied to arouse one's dormant higher potential — purposeful effort that exerts and then rests into poised, alert repose without inertia; the effort behind spiritual elevation
verifications.classical_associations: ceṣṭā = the effort to arouse dormant potentiality (latent genius -> applied will-force -> expression; else unexpressed). Described as the MAIN CAUSE of BOTH mundane development AND spiritual elevation, operating across the physical, psychic and spiritual spheres. (Scope/significance of the vṛtti — NOT a separate cosmological association.)
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: ga = ceṣṭā vṛtti (effort to arouse dormant potential); its immense value in BOTH the mundane and supramundane spheres. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (restless-can't-stop striving vs poised effort-that-rests / spiritually-elevating will-force) applies the framework's restlessness-vs-poise principle (consistent with the source lexicon); the passage frames ceṣṭā as valuable in both spheres and does not itself label a binding pole.
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='effort / striving' is the bare vṛtti NAME, not a binding distortion; v2 liberating='effort as path to mundane development and spiritual elevation' paraphrases the passage's general VALUE statement about ceṣṭā (both spheres) rather than a distinct liberated mode — a mild value/association-into-pole conflation. v3 adopts the lexicon's crisper restless-vs-poised polarity.

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Mamatā, the vṛtti of love and attachment, is related to time, space and individuality. People praise even the poorest goods made in their own country and criticize the best goods made elsewhere — irrational attachment for a place, a psychic disease (SPACE). A mother who sacrifices everything for her child mercilessly slices living kai fish without feeling, deaf to their agony (INDIVIDUALITY). The mother cow who lovingly licks her calf today kicks it away when it grows tomorrow (TIME). Thus mamatā is limited by the relative factors. Only human beings can make mamatā TRANSCEND the boundaries of time, space and individuality, after persistent and intense effort — impossible for other beings. Gha is the acoustic root of mamatā vṛtti.
verifications.binding: mamatā bounded by the relative factors (time, space, individuality) — partial, possessive 'mine-ness' that clings to its own (own child, own country, own moment) while excluding or even harming what lies outside it
verifications.liberating: mamatā made to TRANSCEND time, space and individuality — love expanded past its relative boundaries into universal affection that holds the loved on an open hand (achievable only by human beings, through persistent, intense effort)
verifications.classical_associations: mamatā is related to time, space and individuality; its bounded form shows as place-attachment (praising one's own poor goods over better foreign ones — a 'psychic disease'), individuality (the mother who cherishes her child yet slices kai fish unmoved), and time (the cow that licks its calf today, kicks it away grown tomorrow). (Illustrations/scope of the vṛtti — not a separate cosmological association.)
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED — and unusually so: gha = mamatā vṛtti (love/attachment); its limitation by time/space/individuality; and that only humans can make it TRANSCEND those boundaries through effort. The binding (bounded attachment) vs liberating (boundary-transcending universal love) split is directly SUPPORTED by the passage's own bounded-vs-transcendent contrast — lighter authored component than most entries.
verifications.v2_drift_note: gha is ABSENT from v2 (bridge-unreachable aspirate — reference-only). English G2P has no /gh/ phoneme; written 'gh' yields /g/ -> ga (or is silent, e.g. 'rough'), so gha cannot arise in an English varṇa sequence.

verifications.english_equivalent: the velar nasal /ŋ/ — the 'ng' sound (sing, king, long, song); bridge maps the /ŋ/ phoneme -> nga. BRIDGE-REACHABLE (e.g. longing -> la, nga, nga; king -> ka, nga).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Uṋa (ṅa) is the acoustic root of dambha vṛtti (vanity). The popular story: the sage Vashiṣṭha travelled to China to learn the Chinese school of Tantra, learned the use of una in Tantric mantras, and introduced it in India; una is used extensively across the Indo-Chinese languages (Tibetan, Ladakhi, Sherpa, Manpa). Its transmission is linked to the Tárā cult, trifurcated as Ugra/Vajra Tárā (India), Nīla Tárā / Nīla Sarasvatī (Tibet), and Bhrāmarī / Kṛṣṇa Tárā (China). The acoustic root of Vajra Tárā and Nīla Tárā is aeṃ; that of the black Bhrāmarī Tárā (= Kālī in Varṇāśrama Dharma) is krīṃ (ka = Kārya Brahma + ra = the luminous factor).
verifications.binding: dambha as vanity — the self displayed and performed for others' eyes; conduct staged to be seen and admired
verifications.liberating: conduct that stands without outward performance — action done for its own sake, needing no audience or applause
verifications.classical_associations: Phonetic-historical (NOT poles): per the legend, una was learned by Vashiṣṭha in China and introduced to India, and is used across the Indo-Chinese languages (Tibetan/Ladakhi/Sherpa/Manpa). Its transmission is tied to the Tárā cult — but the Tárā deities have their OWN acoustic roots (aeṃ for Vajra/Nīla Tárā; krīṃ = ka[Kārya Brahma] + ra[luminous factor] for Bhrāmarī Tárā / Kālī), NOT una. Record as history/association; do not fold aeṃ/krīṃ/Tárā into nga's poles.
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: nga (uṋa/ṅa) = dambha vṛtti (vanity); the phonetic history (Chinese-origin legend, Indo-Chinese usage) and the Tárā-cult context with the deities' SEPARATE roots aeṃ/krīṃ. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (displayed-for-others vs conduct-without-performance) applies the framework's display-vs-unselfconscious principle (consistent with the source lexicon); the passage states the vṛtti but does not itself split it into poles.
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='vanity / pride-display' is close to attested, but v2 liberating='egoic obstruction; humility is its spiritual correction' restates the vṛtti's PROBLEM and names its corrective (humility) rather than giving the liberated MODE of conduct. v3 adopts the lexicon's crisper 'conduct that stands without outward performance.' (nga is bridge-reachable — this revises packets for ng-words such as longing/king/song.)

verifications.english_equivalent: the affricate /tʃ/ — the 'ch' sound (church, chair, match); bridge maps ch -> ca. BRIDGE-REACHABLE (church -> ca, ra, ca).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: 'Ca is the acoustic root of viveka [conscience].' — This is the ENTIRE classical passage: it attests ONLY the vṛtti name. No binding/liberating contrast and no further associations are given.
verifications.binding: viveka distorted — discernment hardening into judgmentalism / separation-pride (discrimination used to feel superior to others)
verifications.liberating: falsehood-discerning insight without egoic superiority — clear conscience distinguishing real from unreal, held without pride

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Ṭa is the acoustic root of vitarka vṛtti (overstating one's case). Vitarka is not merely debating; it means overstating one's case to the point of garrulousness — a combination of bad temper and garrulousness. It is NOT synonymous with kaśāya vṛtti (speaking harshly to hurt others). Example (Howrah station): asked whether the Uluberia local has left, one gentleman snaps abusively ('Am I a railway timetable?... People like you make life hell...') — uncontrolled vitarka; a second replies helpfully with just the relevant facts (platform eleven, five minutes) — pramita vāk (balanced statement, only relevant words).

verifications.liberating: pramita vāk — balanced, measured speech using only relevant words; saying just what is warranted (the helpful, to-the-point reply)

verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Ṭha is the acoustic root of anutāpa vṛtti (repentance). One is seized by repentance on realizing (from within, or with a second person's help) the impropriety of one's action. In northern India anutāpa is called paścāttāpa. Anu and paschāt both mean 'later / after'; tāpa means 'heat' (so repentance = 'after-heat').
verifications.binding: anutāpa as gripping remorse — the 'after-heat' that torments, replaying one's own past wrong without release
verifications.liberating: repentance discharged into acceptance — the remorse over one's past act released, the realization-of-impropriety turned into amendment rather than endless self-torment
verifications.classical_associations: COSMOLOGICAL (from the ha passage): ṭha is the acoustic root of nighttime, the moon, bhúvarloka, and the kāmamaya kośa — the contractive OPPOSITE of ha (day/sun/svarloka/parā-vidyā). ETYMOLOGY: anutāpa = anu ('after') + tāpa ('heat'); N. Indian paścāttāpa = paschāt ('after') + tāpa ('heat') = 'after-heat'. verifications.english_equivalent: liquid /r/ -> ra; BRIDGE-REACHABLE and extremely common (any /r/).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Ra is the acoustic root of agnitattva (the fire element) / prāṇaśakti (vitality) — 'Raṃ bījaṃ śikhinaṃ dhyāyet, trikoṇam-aruṇaprabham' (the RAM bīja, triangular, red-glowing). It is ALSO the acoustic root of sarvanāśa (the thought of annihilation): 'I have nothing of my own, everything is gone, I am undone.' Its cure is the constant auto-suggestion 'Parama Puruṣa is mine' (guru mantra); the feeling of defeat is ra-bījātmak, its cure the auto-suggestion 'I have come to win, I am destined to win.' Ra also means 'fire' (the monosyllable ra = fire).
verifications.binding: sarvanāśa — the defeatist annihilation-thought ('I have nothing, everything is gone, I am undone'); destructive collapse, the sense of total defeat
verifications.liberating: prāṇaśakti — the fire of life-force directed as vitality and winning resolve ('I have come to win, I am destined to win'; 'Parama Puruṣa is mine'); directed energy without bondage
verifications.classical_associations: ra = agnitattva (the fire element) and prāṇaśakti (vitality); the RAM bīja mantra (triangular, red-glowing — 'Raṃ bījaṃ śikhinaṃ dhyāyet'); the monosyllable ra = 'fire'. Cure / liberating direction: the auto-suggestion 'Parama Puruṣa is mine' (guru mantra) and 'I am destined to win.' Classical side is DUAL (vitality AND annihilation).
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED — both poles: sarvanāśa (defeatism) as binding and the vital/winning cure (prāṇaśakti / 'I am destined to win' / 'Parama Puruṣa is mine') as the liberating direction; plus the agni/prāṇaśakti/RAM/fire associations. Light authored component (the pole split is in the source; ra is classically DUAL).

verifications.sanskrit_label: Krūratā (cruelty) — with kṣititattva (earth / solid factor) association
verifications.english_equivalent: liquid /l/ -> la; BRIDGE-REACHABLE and extremely common (any /l/).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: La is the acoustic root of kruratā vṛtti (cruelty), counteracted by the propensity of compassion (seeing another's misery: 'what great misery he suffers; can I reduce it? how crude he is in thought and behaviour — can I help arouse his latent intellect?'). La is ALSO the acoustic root of kṣititattva, the solid factor — 'Laṃ bījaṃ dharaṇīṃ dhyāyet, caturasrāṃ supītābhām' (the LAM bīja, four-sided/square, deep-yellow).
verifications.binding: kruratā — cruelty: physical harm inflicted on the weak; crude, cruel thought and behaviour
verifications.liberating: compassion (karuṇā) that protects the vulnerable — the counter-measure to cruelty; the will to reduce another's misery and help arouse their latent intellect
verifications.classical_associations: la = kṣititattva (the solid / earth factor, dharaṇī / pṛthvī); the LAM bīja mantra (four-sided/square, deep-yellow — 'Laṃ bījaṃ dharaṇīṃ dhyāyet'). ('Earth-bound hardness' echoes this solid factor.) An element/bīja association, distinct from the kruratā pole.
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED — both poles: kruratā (cruelty) as binding and compassion/karuṇā as the explicit counter-measure (liberating); plus the kṣititattva/earth + LAM bīja associations. Light authored component.
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='cruelty' is fine; v2 liberating='earth-bound hardness; compassion softens it' makes TWO errors — it FOLDS the kṣititattva (earth/solid) ASSOCIATION into the pole ('earth-bound hardness', association-as-pole) AND names a corrective ('compassion softens it') rather than the liberated MODE. v3 keeps earth/solid as an association and uses the lexicon's 'compassion that protects the physically vulnerable' (= the attested karuṇā counter-measure). Distinct from ddha (piśunatā, sadistic cruelty). la is bridge-reachable and extremely common (/l/).

verifications.sanskrit_label: Dharma (ensconcement in one's original stance / that which sustains) — with jalatattva (water) association; classical side liberating-oriented
verifications.english_equivalent: labial approximant -> va; BRIDGE-REACHABLE and common. Note: English MERGES /v/ (van) and /w/ (win/water) both to va (Sanskrit व covers both).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Va is the acoustic root of dharma — 'ensconcement in one's original stance'. The innate propensity of human beings is to move toward subtlety in the psychic/spiritual spheres and finally merge into Parama Puruṣa; this unbroken movement is mānava dharma. 'Sukhaṃ vāñchati sarvo hi... ' (all beings long for happiness; dharma originates from that innate propensity, so dharma should be observed by all). 'Dhriyate dharma ityāhuḥ' — dharma is that which SUSTAINS. To diverge from dharma is to rush toward total annihilation. Va is ALSO the acoustic root of jalatattva (the liquid factor — water and any liquid) and of the rain-god Varuṇa Deva.
verifications.binding: ensconcement gone rigid — over-holding, clinging to one's holding; stuck fixity that resists the movement toward subtlety
verifications.liberating: dharma — ensconcement in one's original (true) stance; the sustaining principle ('that which sustains'), the unbroken movement toward subtlety and merger into Parama Puruṣa (mānava dharma)
verifications.classical_associations: va = jalatattva (the liquid factor — water and any liquid) and the rain-god Varuṇa Deva. Dharma = 'that which sustains' (dhriyate dharma); the innate longing for happiness is its origin ('sukhaṃ vāñchati sarvo hi'); diverging from dharma rushes toward annihilation. (Element/deity association, distinct from the dharma pole.)
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED (primary text): va = dharma = ENSCONCEMENT in one's original stance + 'that which sustains' + movement toward subtlety/Parama Puruṣa; plus the jalatattva/water + Varuṇa association; classical side liberating-oriented. The binding (rigid over-holding) is the distortion of ensconcement. Light authored component.
verifications.v2_drift_note: REVERSAL — here v2 is MORE text-faithful than the lexicon. v2 (binding='rigid/stuck ensconcement, clinging to holding'; liberating='dharma, sustaining flow, movement toward subtlety') matches the primary text's dharma-as-ensconcement/sustaining. The LEXICON drifts (bind='accepting-as-true without discernment'; lib='truth-assent purified by discernment') — a narrower truth-assent framing NOT supported by THIS passage. v3 follows the PRIMARY TEXT (≈ v2). This corrects the earlier generalization that v2 is uniformly the weaker source: for va the LEXICON is the weaker one. va is bridge-reachable and common (/v/,/w/).

verifications.sanskrit_label: Kāma (physical / worldly desire) — with tamoguṇa (the static principle) association
verifications.english_equivalent: palatal sibilant /ʃ/ ('sh') -> sha; BRIDGE-REACHABLE (ship/shine/wish).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Śa is the acoustic root of tamoguṇa (the static principle), and also of all kinds of worldly desires — wealth, opulence, name, fame, social position. The collective Sanskrit term is kāma. The four recognized longings of human life are dharma (psycho-spiritual), artha (psychic), kāma (PHYSICAL), and mokṣa (spiritual / liberation). kāma = all types of PHYSICAL longings.
verifications.binding: kāma — worldly / physical desire and longing: grasping for wealth, opulence, name, fame, social position; the tamasic pull toward the crude
verifications.liberating: physical longing sublimated / redirected toward the higher — desire turned from kāma toward mokṣa (the longing for liberation); worldly grasping released
verifications.classical_associations: śa = tamoguṇa (the static principle). The four puruṣārthas (longings): dharma (psycho-spiritual), artha (psychic), kāma (physical), mokṣa (liberation) — kāma = all physical longings. (Guṇa association + longing-hierarchy frame.)
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED (primary text): śa = TAMOGUṆA (static principle) + KĀMA (all PHYSICAL worldly desires); the four-puruṣārtha frame. BINDING pole (kāma) attested. AUTHORED: the LIBERATING pole (sublimation toward mokṣa) is inferred from the puruṣārtha hierarchy, not stated as a pole.
verifications.v2_drift_note: MAJOR DISCREPANCY — BOTH v2 AND the lexicon MIS-ASSIGN śa's guṇa and puruṣārtha. Primary text: śa = TAMOGUṆA (static) + KĀMA (physical longing). But the lexicon = 'rajoguṇa + artha' and v2 = 'mutative drive / rajas / artha' — i.e. BOTH say RAJAS (mutative) + ARTHA (psychic), a different guṇa AND a different puruṣārtha (artha=psychic ≠ kāma=physical). v3 follows the PRIMARY TEXT (tamoguṇa + kāma). SIBILANT SWAP CONFIRMED (see the sa/ssa passage): the derived tables SWAP palatal śa (sha, correctly kāma/tamoguṇa) and retroflex ṣa (ssa, correctly artha/rajoguṇa) — they filed rajoguṇa/artha under sha and kāma/tamoguṇa under ssa. sa (mokṣa/sattva) is correct in both. sha is bridge-reachable (/ʃ/).

verifications.sanskrit_label: Mokṣa (unqualified liberation / salvation) — with sattvaguṇa (the sentient principle) association; classical side liberating-oriented
verifications.english_equivalent: dental sibilant /s/ -> sa; BRIDGE-REACHABLE and extremely common (any /s/).
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar: Sa is the acoustic root of mokṣa (salvation, unqualified liberation) and of sattvaguṇa (the sentient principle). In the four-varga scheme: va = dharma (+ liquid factor); ṣa ('sha') = artha (removal of worldly wants) + rajoguṇa; śa = kāma (worldly/physical wants) + tamoguṇa; sa = mokṣa + sattvaguṇa.
verifications.binding: the sentient / sattvic impulse clung to — clarity, purity or harmony owned as superiority or attachment (the subtle 'golden chain' of spiritual attainment)
verifications.liberating: mokṣa — unqualified liberation; sentient clarity realized WITHOUT attachment to it ('clarity without attachment to clarity')
verifications.classical_associations: sa = sattvaguṇa (the sentient principle) and mokṣa (unqualified liberation) — the highest of the four longings (dharma/artha/kāma/mokṣa). Part of the four-varga sibilant scheme: śa(sha)=tamoguṇa/kāma, ṣa(ssa)=rajoguṇa/artha, sa=sattvaguṇa/mokṣa.
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED (primary text): sa = mokṣa (unqualified liberation) + sattvaguṇa (sentient principle); classical side liberating-oriented. AUTHORED: the binding pole (sattva clung to as purity/superiority — the golden chain) is lexicon-supplied but a standard reading of sattvic attachment; liberating = mokṣa / clarity-without-attachment.
verifications.v2_drift_note: v2 liberating='sattva; clarity; peace; release; mokṣa; unqualified liberation' is CORRECT (matches the primary text); v2 binding='escapism; premature static withdrawal; inert/static withdrawal' drifts toward a TAMASIC withdrawal reading rather than sattva's subtle attachment (the golden chain). v3 uses the lexicon's 'clarity without attachment to clarity.' sa is CORRECTLY assigned in both tables (unlike sha/ssa which are swapped). sa is bridge-reachable and extremely common (/s/).

verifications.sanskrit_label: Artha (psychic longing / worldly purpose — removal of worldly wants) — with rajoguṇa (the mutative principle) association
verifications.english_equivalent: retroflex sibilant ṣa (ष). PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE: bridge target fed by 'shr' (never emitted); English /ʃ/ -> sha (palatal), so the retroflex ṣa never arises.
verifications.source_quote: Sarkar (four-varga passage): ṣa ('sha') is the acoustic root of artha — 'the removal of worldly wants' — and of rajoguṇa (the mutative principle). artha is the PSYCHIC longing among the four (dharma/artha/kāma/mokṣa).
verifications.binding: artha as possessive acquisition — worldly purpose pursued and possessed as acquisition, status or control (rajasic grasping to acquire)
verifications.liberating: purposeful action without possessive bondage — rajasic energy directed to legitimate purpose/means without clinging (artha pursued without attachment)
verifications.classical_associations: ṣa = rajoguṇa (the mutative principle); artha = the psychic longing / the means that removes worldly wants. Part of the four-varga sibilant scheme (śa=tamoguṇa/kāma, ṣa=rajoguṇa/artha, sa=sattva/mokṣa).
verifications.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED (primary text): ṣa = artha (psychic longing / worldly purpose, 'removal of worldly wants') + rajoguṇa (mutative principle). AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (possessive acquisition vs purposeful action without bondage) is lexicon-supplied — and these pole texts are taken from the lexicon's MIS-FILED 'sha' entry (see swap).
verifications.v2_drift_note: SIBILANT SWAP CONFIRMED. Primary text: retroflex ṣa (ssa) = artha + RAJOGUṆA; palatal śa (sha) = kāma + TAMOGUṆA. But BOTH derived tables SWAP them: they file kāma/tamoguṇa under ssa (v2 'static inertia / tamas-bound kama'; lexicon 'Kāma/Tamoguṇa') and rajoguṇa/artha under sha. v3 corrects by following the primary text: ssa = artha/rajoguṇa (pole texts from the lexicon's mis-filed 'sha' content), sha = kāma/tamoguṇa. ssa is PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE (retroflex; 'shr' never emitted).
